terms.grammar: adverb, with adjectives and adverbs: satis bene, satis bonus
evidence: Cic. Off. 3.58: nec īnfacētus et satis litterātus
terms.comment: Like English “enough”, satis can lower a quality: “tolerably, pretty, fairly” (Lewis & Short); satis bene, quite well.

terms.grammar: adverb; with a genitive, quite a lot of
evidence: Cic. Div. 2.3: mihi quidem ipsī sānē aliquantum medētur (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Latin also says “rather” with the comparative (longior, rather long) or with sub-: subtristis, rather glum (Ter. And. 447); subdifficilis, rather hard (Cic. Amic. 67).

phrases.english: not without wit, and quite well read

phrases.latin: respondit: ‘bene pāscere’; quid secundum: ‘satis bene pāscere’
phrases.english: he answered, “good grazing”; and second best? “quite good grazing”

phrases.latin: Subtristis vīsus est esse aliquantulum mihi.
phrases.english: He seemed to me a little on the glum side.

sources: Lewis & Short: satis · Lewis & Short: aliquantus (aliquantum) · Lewis & Short: subtristis · Lewis & Short: subdifficilis
